alternatives: - **A per-domain fetcher-callback hook** (mirroring `@cellarnode/ui`'s `usePackagingOptions({ fetcher })`) — rejected: the consumer still owns the URL, so the three call sites would keep diverging on path shape; the point of this ticket is for the row, not the caller, to own that. - **Derive `ReferenceDataRow` configs generically from the vendored canonical JSON at runtime** — rejected per the standing CEL-1604 decision: no bundler can prove that derivation pure, so it would pull the 157 KB vendored JSON into every consumer's bundle. - **Migrate all three consumers in this same PR** — rejected: this package hasn't released yet, so a consumer migration today would target an unpublished version; sequencing per the component-library workflow (lib first, release, then consumers).
consequences: Every dashboard that needs a reference-data row going forward writes a `ReferenceDataRow` config instead of a bespoke fetcher; admin and producer each delete their own fetch/parse logic once they migrate, keeping only their `transport`. Until that follow-up PR lands, the classification data path has FOUR implementations in the workspace (three old, one new) rather than one — an accepted, time-boxed duplication cost in exchange for shipping the hook without a cross-repo lockstep release. `useReferenceData` is a new public surface every dashboard can now depend on for any future canonical row, not only classification.
context: The canonical classification taxonomy (`beverage_classifications`) reached dashboards through three independently hand-rolled fetchers: this package's own `useBeverageLabelMap` (public API, builds a label map), admin-dashboard-v2's `use-classification-options.ts` (same-origin `/admin/reference-data/:dataId`), and producer-dashboard's `useClassifications.ts` (cross-origin `/api/v1/classifications/beverage-types` via a typed OpenAPI client). Each duck-types the `{ jsonData: { categories }, version }` envelope slightly differently and has its own loading/error/fallback behaviour. Spec `docs/specs/2026-09-02-matching-canonical-deepening.md` §2 card 09 ("Dashboard client"), D13, calls for one hook where transport is the only thing that varies between a same-origin admin caller and a cross-origin public caller. CEL-1604 (accepted 2026-09-03, same repo) had already established that a hook's static fallback must never import the vendored 157 KB `src/canonical/reference-data.json` — only the generated `classifications.generated.ts` literal is safe to reach at runtime.
decision: Add `useReferenceData(row, { transport })` (`src/react/use-reference-data.ts`). `ReferenceDataTransport` carries `kind: "admin" | "public"`, `baseUrl`, `fetchFn`, `requestInit` — everything that differs between a same-origin admin caller and a cross-origin public caller. `ReferenceDataRow<T>` carries `dataId`, per-kind `paths`, a `parse()` that returns `null` on any unrecognised shape, and a static `fallback`. `data` is always a usable value (the fallback while loading/erroring/malformed), matching `@cellarnode/ui`'s existing `usePackagingOptions` contract. The one shipped row this PR wires up is `CLASSIFICATION_REFERENCE_ROW` (`src/react/classification-reference-row.ts`), whose fallback is `getCanonicalClassifications()` — never the vendored JSON — plus `useBeverageClassifications()` as a thin convenience wrapper. Classification also gains the `is` / `normalizeAndCheck` / `getEntry` functions (`src/classifications.ts`) the other canonical vocabularies already have, scoped per-category for subtypes. The three replaced fetchers are NOT edited in this PR — `useBeverageLabelMap` keeps its exact existing contract for its current consumers; the migration is a follow-up PR once this package releases.
title: One parameterised reference-data hook serves every dashboard; transport is the only adapter
